clue.text: Show amateur and great poet using the same metre

indicators.note: the two pieces share a single metre symbol where they meet, so the doubled one is dropped

blocks.note: a ham is an amateur, especially a radio enthusiast or poor actor
John Milton, author of Paradise Lost

explanation.surface: A reviewer notes that an amateur production and a great poet share the same verse metre.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the abbreviation for metre; one M serves both words, as the clue says.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamilton is the hit Broadway musical about Alexander Hamilton, so it is a stage show.

clue.text: Try to make perfect street straight

blocks.note: to hone is to refine towards perfection
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Someone works hard to make a street perfectly straight.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Straight' can mean frank and truthful, a synonym of honest.

clue.text: Convoy's way blocked by tense whales

indicators.note: something blocked has other things stuck in its middle

blocks.note: a mode is a way or manner
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
orcas are killer whales

explanation.surface: A convoy's road is blocked by whales, of all things.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is', joining definition to wordplay; 'way' is a manner, not a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcade is a procession of cars, which is a kind of convoy.

clue.text: Start of novel, say: two space travellers back from Mars make a fast buck

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, so only that is taken

blocks.note: the opening line of a book is line one
Mr Spock of Star Trek and ET, the alien of the Spielberg film
the last letter of Mars

explanation.surface: A novel opens with two space travellers returning from Mars, and the author cashes in.
explanation.walkthrough: Lining one's pockets is profiting, often dishonestly.
explanation.definitionFit: To line one's pockets is an idiom for making money quickly, often improperly.

clue.text: Victim of eviction stirred us to act

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters get jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Seeing someone evicted moved us to take action.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is someone cast out or rejected, as an evicted person is thrown out.

clue.text: Lavish drink on sons at uni

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to lap is to drink as a cat does
a student at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: Students splash out on drinks while away at university.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'drink on sons' puts the drink after the sons. Being 'up' at university is a British idiom, especially for Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap-up meal is a lavish, generous feast, so the hyphenated adjective means lavish.

clue.text: Olive on an ID card represented Italian oil producer

indicators.note: to represent is to depict anew, so the letters are set out in another form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An olive pictured on an identity card stands for an Italian olive oil maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil producer' suggests olive oil, but means a painter in oils.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was an Italian Renaissance painter whose works, like the Mona Lisa, are oil paintings.

clue.text: Load piano having turned lever on it

indicators.note: something turned round faces the opposite way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to lade is to load cargo
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: Movers load a piano, turning it over with a lever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' in the definition refers back to the piano, whose pedals are foot levers.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano pedal is a foot-operated lever on the instrument.

clue.text: Blighter hazards that woman has no end of goodwill

indicators.note: having no end of a word means its final letter is taken away from the other piece

blocks.note: perils are hazards
the last letter of goodwill, to be dropped
a pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A rogue endangers a woman who has no goodwill left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of goodwill' sounds like plenty of goodwill, but it strips that word's last letter from the hazards. 'Perisher' is old British slang for a pest or rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang insults for an annoying or mischievous person, especially a child.

clue.text: Customer with right to a lawyer in court

indicators.note: one piece sitting in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
to a lawyer, a lien is a right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A customer has the right to legal representation in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right to a lawyer' sounds like a defendant's entitlement but is a definition of a legal claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is a customer of a professional such as a lawyer.

clue.text: Unacceptable idea I must abandon

indicators.note: abandoning something means leaving it behind, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: a notion is an idea
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: Someone is told to drop an idea because it simply will not do.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the I from NOTION leaves NOT ON.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Not on' is a British idiom for something not allowed or socially unacceptable.

clue.text: Monks wanting extra-long cassocks, an unreasonable request?

blocks.note: surface reading: a monastery placing an awkward clothing request
setter's reading: monks needing long robes would be a religious community of lanky men

explanation.surface: A tailor faces a monastery whose monks all want extra-long cassocks.
explanation.walkthrough: Monks form a religious order, and monks who need extra-long cassocks must be tall ones; the phrase for a very demanding request falls out.
explanation.definitionFit: A 'tall order' is an idiom for a request that is difficult or unreasonable to fulfil.

clue.text: Replacement Eurostar terminal in Barking planned

indicators.note: a terminal is the end point, so only the final letter of the following word is used
something planned is arranged, so the letters are put into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of Barking

explanation.surface: A replacement train terminal for Eurostar is being planned in Barking, a district of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminal' sounds like a railway terminus, but here it means the end letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A surrogate is a substitute that stands in for someone or something else.

clue.text: Reference book finally abridged

indicators.note: an abridged text is shortened, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: 'at last' means finally

explanation.surface: A reference book has at last been shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' looks like it selects a last letter, but it is the phrase AT LAST, which then loses its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a book of maps consulted for geographical reference.

clue.text: Seconds from splashdown, take shelter for inventor's protection

indicators.note: seconds here are the second letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: second letters of splashdown and take
a tent is a shelter

explanation.surface: Seconds after a capsule's splashdown, the astronauts take shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' looks like time, but means second letters, taken from two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A patent legally protects an inventor's rights to an invention.

clue.text: Swimmer finishing with a strong kick, then getting out?

blocks.clueFragment: Swimmer finishing with a strong kick, then getting out?
blocks.note: surface reading: a competitive swimmer sprinting to the wall then climbing out of the pool

blocks.clueFragment: Swimmer finishing with a strong kick, then getting out?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a young amphibian that ends its swimming stage by growing kicking legs and leaving the water

explanation.surface: A race swimmer kicks hard to finish and then hauls out of the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: The young of a frog swims with a tail, finishes that stage by growing powerful legs, then leaves the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the aquatic larval form of a frog or toad, which swims before it develops legs.

clue.text: Brainy fellow going to round up vote for Democratic Party

indicators.note: to round up is to gather in and enclose

blocks.note: an event that is going ahead is on
a voter marks a ballot with a cross
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for Democratic
a do is a party

explanation.surface: An intellectual canvasses support for the Democratic Party.
explanation.walkthrough: XFORDDO goes inside ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford don is a university fellow at Oxford, a byword for a brainy academic.

clue.text: Idiot seeing trespass hired gun

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
'seeing' can mean since or because, like as
a trespass is a sin, as in the Lord's Prayer

explanation.surface: A fool who spots an intruder hires a gunman.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired gun is a paid killer, which is what an assassin is.

clue.text: Waiting agent strips again in the mirror

indicators.note: a mirror image runs the other way, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: to repeel is to strip again

explanation.surface: A secret agent waits, stripping off again in front of the mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper is a spy planted to live quietly until activated, so a dormant waiting agent.

clue.text: Cancel drive back having received answer

indicators.note: a word that has received something holds it inside

blocks.note: to repel is to drive back
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Someone calls off a return drive after getting a reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a reversal signal but belongs inside the phrase 'drive back'.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke or cancel it.

clue.text: Fury on both sides faced with PM's change

indicators.note: both sides of a word are its two outside letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: Narendra Modi is India's Prime Minister; the 's is read as 'is', linking to the definition
the first and last letters of Fury

explanation.surface: A prime minister faces fury from both sides of the house over a policy change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faced with' puts the PM's name in front of the fury letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To modify something is to alter or change it.

clue.text: Married ladies corrected cards handed out in error

indicators.note: correcting something changes it around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for married
taken as written

explanation.surface: Married ladies set right a card game where the hands were given out wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: A misdeal is a wrong distribution of cards by the dealer, which must be redone.

clue.text: Left in charge, Charlie cleared out winter clothing

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it
a word cleared out has its insides emptied, leaving only its outside letters

blocks.note: a fee is a charge
L is the abbreviation for left
the first and last letters of Charlie

explanation.surface: A man left in charge, Charlie, clears out the winter wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside FEE. Charlie is the NATO-alphabet C, but here the word itself is emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleece is a warm synthetic jacket worn in cold weather.

clue.text: Vehicle with trailer reversing it through bend

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the word is read the other way round
one piece going through another sits inside it

blocks.note: an arc is a bend or curve
taken as written

explanation.surface: A driver reverses an articulated lorry around a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversing' fits a lorry driver's manoeuvre, but it turns the word 'it' around.
explanation.definitionFit: An artic is a British short form of articulated lorry, a cab unit towing a trailer.

clue.text: Warm fabric undesirable for gardener with temperature up

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for temperature
a weed is an unwanted plant

explanation.surface: A warm fabric is unsuitable for a gardener when the temperature rises.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'up' puts the temperature letter above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is a thick woollen cloth, valued for warmth.

clue.text: Send ampoule containing end of applicator, having had Covid?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so that is the one kept
containing means holding something inside

blocks.note: to post is to send
a vial is a small medicine bottle like an ampoule
the final letter of applicator

explanation.surface: Instructions for posting a medical ampoule to someone recovering from Covid.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags Covid as one example of a virus, so the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Post-viral describes the condition after a viral infection, and Covid is one such infection.

clue.text: East Coast mainline station still widening platform

indicators.note: a thing widening spreads out around what lies inside it

blocks.note: a stage is a raised platform
'even' can mean still, as in 'even better'

explanation.surface: A station on Britain's East Coast line is still having its platform widened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Platform' seems to belong with the station, but it is the outer piece. Stevenage is a Hertfordshire town on the main line north from London.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenage has a railway station on the East Coast Main Line out of London King's Cross.

clue.text: Poke for one horse from behind

indicators.note: starting from the back means reading the letters right to left

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, or 'for one'
a dun is a greyish-brown horse

explanation.surface: Someone jabs a horse from behind to get it going.
explanation.definitionFit: To nudge is to prod or poke someone gently, often with an elbow.

clue.text: Rolling in mud, soldiers initially practice without kit

indicators.note: rolling things tumble over, so the letters are tossed into a new order
initially points to the first letter of the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers rolling in mud on an exercise, practising without their kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Practice' looks like military training, but it means a way of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudism is the practice of going naked, that is, wearing no clothing at all.

clue.text: Casual affair saving daughter's marriage, perhaps

indicators.note: saving can mean except, so the named letter is left out

blocks.note: a dalliance is a casual romantic affair
D is the abbreviation for daughter; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A fling might save a daughter's marriage, a wry thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' seems to mean rescuing, but here it means except.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is one example of an alliance, a union between two parties.
